data.name: Time-Based Greeting Pipeline
data.description: A simple 3-step pipeline that fetches the current time, generates a friendly greeting with the timestamp, and echoes it back.

input_variables.name: timezone
input_variables.description: Timezone for the greeting (e.g. 'UTC', 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London'). Defaults to UTC if not provided.

example_prompts: Generate a friendly greeting with the current time
Create a time-based greeting for New York timezone
Get current time and make a greeting message

arguments.prompt: Generate a single-line friendly greeting that incorporates this timestamp: {{get_time.datetime}}. Make it warm and conversational.
arguments.system_prompt: You are a friendly assistant. Generate exactly one line of greeting text that naturally incorporates the given timestamp. Be warm and conversational.

arguments.prompt: Echo this greeting exactly as written: {{generate_greeting.response}}
arguments.system_prompt: You are an echo service. Return the input text exactly as provided, with no modifications or additions.

suggestions: Replace the 'echo_greeting' node with a simple output/return node that takes the greeting from 'generate_greeting' as the final pipeline result
If an echo tool exists in the available tools, use that instead of 'llm_call' for step 3
Ensure step 2 (generate_greeting) has a prompt that instructs the LLM to use the timestamp from {{get_time.__all__}} and generate exactly one line
Verify that step 3 correctly references the output from step 2 using the appropriate template variable like {{generate_greeting.__all__}}
validation_issues: Step 3 uses 'llm_call' tool for echoing, but echoing doesn't require an LLM - this is inefficient and semantically incorrect
The 'echo' functionality should use a simpler tool or be the final output of the pipeline rather than requiring a separate LLM call
No validation that the greeting from step 2 is properly passed to step 3
